w10_T4_004125: A tile-maker loaded 98 racks into the kiln, and each rack held 5 tiles. A neighbouring workshop sent 77 finished tiles to join the batch, and 26 more were salvaged from an old order. A big hotel contract then tripled the number of tiles in the store. During transport 233 tiles were cracked and thrown away. The workshop's delivery van has done 64000 miles. How many tiles does the tile-maker have now?
w10_T4_004128: A charity shop had 163 paperbacks on its shelves, and a house clearance brought in 49 more. The manager split the paperbacks evenly into 2 equal piles, sent one pile to the sister shop, and kept the other. From the pile she kept, 93 books were sold over the weekend. A publisher then donated 3 copies of every book still in that pile. How many books are in that pile now?
w10_T4_004131: A phone shop received 33 boxes of chargers, and each box held 9 chargers. A fault recall took 49 chargers off the shelf, and 126 were sold in the first week. A returned order put 44 chargers back. The shop quotes charging times in minutes although the boxes are labelled in hours, and the branch has 7 members of staff. How many chargers are in the shop now?
w10_T4_004136: On Monday morning a scout hall had 24 tent poles, which were shared equally between the 6 patrols; the beaver patrol's share is the one being followed. Before lunch the quartermaster issued 3 more poles for every pole that patrol held. In the afternoon a supplier delivered a further 4 poles for each pole in the patrol's store. Later the patrol split its poles evenly into 2 identical kit bags and took just one bag to camp. In the evening the camp store matched that bag over and over, leaving the patrol with 6 poles for every pole in it. The hall is booked for 90 minutes each Tuesday although the rota shows the booking in hours. How many tent poles does the patrol have at camp?
w10_T4_004144: Elena and Marco run a puzzle library, and Marco always has fewer jigsaws out on loan than Elena. Elena catalogued 171 jigsaws and bought 19 more at auction. A grant then funded 5 copies of every jigsaw she held. The collection was shared equally between the 5 branch libraries, and the riverside branch's share is the one to follow. Marco later donated 55 jigsaws to the riverside branch. How many jigsaws does the riverside branch have?
w10_T4_004147: A council depot began the year with 221 rolls of pavement tape, of which 137 went to the highways team and 23 perished in the damp. A supplier then delivered 50 rolls. Each roll was cut into 8 lengths, and every length was cut again into 8 short strips. The strips were shared equally between the 6 area teams, and the north team's share is the one being followed. The depot measures tape in metres although the invoices are written in centimetres. How many strips does the north team have?
w10_T4_004148: On Monday morning Ivan cracked 129 crates of walnuts, and each crate produced 9 bags of kernels. Before noon 1036 bags were sent to the wholesaler, and 28 bags were rejected as mouldy in the early afternoon. Later that afternoon Ivan's brother Petro, who always packs fewer bags than Ivan does, ran the line again and turned out 7 bags for every bag Ivan still had. In the evening a supermarket collected 330 bags. How many bags does Ivan have left?
w10_T4_004152: Leah keeps more chickens than her neighbour Sam. She started the month with 29 hens, sold 12 at the market, and hatched 59 chicks that joined the flock. A friend then gave her 50 more birds. Every bird laid 9 eggs during the month, and Sam added 47 eggs of his own to her crates. A wholesaler asked for a repeat batch, so Leah supplied 2 eggs for every egg she had counted. The farm shop prices eggs in dollars although the wholesaler quotes in cents. How many eggs did Leah supply in the end?
w10_T4_004155: Early on Saturday morning a market stall had 25 punnets of strawberries, and the grower delivered 53 more before opening. A clumsy customer crushed 5 punnets mid-morning. At midday a second grower brought 48 punnets. During the afternoon 93 punnets were sold. In the evening the stallholder repacked the fruit, making 7 small pots out of every punnet still on the table, and a friend added 69 pots she had made at home. How many pots does the stall have?
w10_T4_004156: On Sunday morning a garden centre had 169 bags of compost, and 123 bags were sold before noon. In the afternoon the supplier restocked at a rate of 4 bags for every bag left on the pallet. In the early evening a landscaper returned 68 bags. Overnight the bags were shared equally between the chain's 6 stores, and the town store's share is the one to follow. How many bags went to the town store?
w10_T4_004157: Owen and Freya split a mural project, and Freya paints fewer panels than Owen does. The wall was marked out as 60 panels and shared equally between the 3 painting teams, and Owen's team's share is the one being followed. That share was then divided evenly into 2 identical weeks of work, and only the first week is counted here. Each panel in that week was broken into 8 small mosaic tiles. In the frost 34 tiles cracked, and Freya later supplied 34 replacements. The council describes the job in hours although the painters log it in minutes. How many tiles does Owen's team have for that week?
w10_T4_004160: On Monday morning Delia unloaded 149 rolls of fabric, while her partner Ahmed unloaded fewer than she did. Each roll was cut into 6 lengths before noon. In the early afternoon every length was cut into 4 panels, and by late afternoon each panel had been trimmed into 5 quilting squares. Ahmed added 51 squares from his own stock in the evening. Overnight 2786 squares were dispatched to the shops. How many squares are left?
w10_T4_004162: Nina has more paint rollers than her brother Karl. She started with 17 rollers and threw away 11 that were worn out. The rest were shared equally between the 6 rooms she was decorating, and the kitchen's allocation is the one to follow. For the second coat she ordered 9 rollers for every roller allocated to the kitchen. Karl then ordered 4 rollers for each of those, so the whole house would be covered. The shop quotes drying times in hours although the tins are labelled in minutes. How many rollers are in the final order?
w10_T4_004165: On Friday morning a leisure centre had 168 towels in the laundry, and 79 clean towels came back from the service. Before lunch 179 towels went out to the pool. In the afternoon the manager ordered 4 towels for every towel still in the laundry. During the evening 191 towels were taken by the gym. Late that night 67 towels were dropped back into the laundry basket. Half of the laundry room is taken up by the dryers, and staff shifts are posted in hours although the machines count in minutes. How many towels are in the laundry now?
w10_T4_004171: A vineyard picked 147 baskets of grapes, and each basket filled 9 bottles. A neighbour contributed 46 bottles, and the cellar turned up 47 more from last year. The bottles were divided evenly into 2 equal cellars, and the west cellar is the one being followed. A distributor then ordered 4 bottles for every bottle in the west cellar. How many bottles does that order come to?
w10_T4_004172: On Wednesday morning Dario had 174 tulips ready for the shop, more than his colleague Elsa had managed to cut. He sold 54 tulips before lunch. At midday he gave half of the tulips he had left to Elsa's van and kept the rest. During the afternoon the grower delivered 7 tulips for every tulip Dario was still holding. In the evening those flowers were split evenly into 2 buckets, and only the bucket left in the cold room is counted from here on. Elsa dropped 30 more tulips into that bucket. How many tulips are in the cold room bucket?
w10_T4_004173: On Monday morning a nut factory had 104 sacks of almonds, and a lorry delivered 70 more before noon. In the early afternoon each sack was tipped into 6 barrels. Later that afternoon every barrel was divided into 7 tubs. In the evening each tub was filled out into 5 jars, and overnight every jar was portioned into 3 sachets. How many sachets did the factory end up with?
w10_T4_004174: Bruno bakes more loaves than his cousin Elif does. He mixed 136 batches of dough, and each batch made 5 loaves. The morning rush took 381 loaves. Bruno then opened a second bakery and produced 9 loaves for every loaf he still had. Elif's cafe bought 277 loaves at the end of the day, and half of Bruno's shop front is taken up by the window display. How many loaves does Bruno have now?
w10_T4_004175: A guitar teacher printed 45 booklets, and each booklet contained 9 exercises. The proofreader struck out 23 exercises that had misprints. A colleague then contributed 46 new exercises. The teacher produced a version of the whole book for each of the 4 grades she teaches, using that many exercises in every version. Her studio holds 16 students at a time, and lessons are advertised in hours although she bills them in minutes. How many exercises are there across all the versions together?
w10_T4_004182: Kofi collects more postcards than his friend Marta. He bought 74 albums, and each album already held 5 postcards. Marta gave him 62 postcards from a holiday, and a market stall added 38 more. A collectors' club then arranged a swap that left Kofi with 6 postcards for every postcard he owned. Half of his desk is buried under the collection, and the club lists postage in dollars although the stall prices everything in cents. How many postcards does Kofi have now?
w10_T4_004189: A community kitchen had 63 jars of jam, and a volunteer brought in a dozen more. The jars were shared equally between the 5 lunch clubs, and the harbour club's share is the one to follow. A supermarket then matched the donation, giving the harbour club 4 jars for every jar in its share. The club later divided its jars equally between its 4 tables, and the corner table's share is the one being counted. The kitchen serves 80 meals a week, and it prices its jam in dollars although the labels are printed in cents. How many jars are on the corner table?
w10_T4_004190: A cinema had 144 free passes for Saturday morning. By noon 129 passes had been claimed at the box office. In the afternoon 6 passes were withdrawn as forgeries, and 2 more were lost. In the evening the chain reissued the surviving passes for each of its 8 screens, printing that many passes per screen. The cinema seats 220 people. How many passes were printed altogether?
w10_T4_004193: A council nursery had 118 trays of saplings, and 69 trays went out to the parks. A donation added 39 trays. Each tray was then split into 3 pots, and every pot was later divided into 6 seedlings. Storm damage killed 558 seedlings, and 299 were given away on community planting day. The nursery has 14 greenhouses, and it measures growth in centimetres although its reports are written in metres. How many seedlings are left?
w10_T4_004195: Rania stocks more soap than her business partner Jonas does. She ordered 182 cases, and each case held 4 boxes. Every box was then opened out into 3 gift sets. Jonas added 22 gift sets from his workshop, and a customer returned 4 more. The sets were shared equally between the 5 shops in the group, and the market square shop's share is the one being followed; Jonas sent 27 extra sets to that shop. The group quotes delivery times in hours although the couriers record them in minutes. How many gift sets does the market square shop have?
w10_T4_004202: A rowing club had 53 oars in the boathouse. A regatta took 34 oars away for the weekend, and 15 more were sent off for repair. The club then bought 4 oars for every oar still in the boathouse. The oars were finally split evenly between the club's 2 racks, and the upper rack's share stayed for training. The boathouse is 26 years old. How many oars are on the upper rack?
